A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the map verification problem can be solved with a constant number of edge markers and in O(|VM |) edge traversals for the plane embedded graph world, and with a constant number (independent of the graph size) of edge markers and O(|VG | × |EG |) edge traversal cost for the general graph world.
we have shown a strategy that verifies the robot's map in O(|VG||VM|) edge-traversals, using a single marker, for a graph world with no overpasses and tunnels.

the mechanical cost for verification of a graph world can be reduced to O(|VM|), even when the graph world is not a planar embedded graph, using a single marker.
the mechanical cost of verifying a map of a graph world depends only on the size of the map and not on the size of world.
